description: Issuing track warrants and track and time authority, CTC control of signaled territory, train sheets, bulletins, and speed restrictions for 61 railroads from the primary and backup NOCs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every train and roadway work group needs movement or work authority. Paper track warrants by radio sustain about 40% of normal train starts in dark territory; CTC territory (1,620 miles) needs signal maintainers at each control point in local control. After 8 hours yards and interchanges back up and Class I connections refuse traffic. RPO is zero because an authority in effect must never be lost (synchronous replication to DC-2)
manual_workaround: Printed bulletins and paper track warrant forms at each dispatch desk; dispatchers issue warrants by radio and record them on paper; signal maintainers take local control of CTC interlockings; priority given to PIH trains and passenger host segments (CR-07 to CR-09)
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-06; SYS-08; SYS-03 (CTC code servers)
dependent_third_parties: CAD software vendor; telecommunications carriers (microwave and leased circuits); Class I dispatch centers (coordination at interchanges)
dependent_people_or_facilities: 310 train dispatchers and supervisors; primary NOC (Florida) and backup NOC (Texas); signal maintainers in 5 regions
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of rail operations revenue ($11.5 million a day) deferred or lost (about $6.9 million) plus about $0.3 million in overtime, crew relief, and car hire
acquired_railroad_dependency: AQ-04 to AQ-06 are dispatched on their own legacy systems (BP-16)
single_points_of_failure: None (hot standby in DC-2); radio and microwave backhaul has single routes to 14 tower sites

business_process: PTC operations on host and tenant territory
description: Office segment of the PTC system for the 212 route miles that CR-07 to CR-09 host for passenger trains; back office for the 236 company locomotives that run on Class I PTC lines; interoperable messaging with Class I and passenger operators
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without the back office, trains on host territory run under the en route failure limits in 49 CFR 236.1029(b) and the PTCSP, and the passenger operators may cancel trains. New tenant trains cannot initialize, so 22 railroads cannot enter Class I PTC lines (236.1006(a)). After 8 hours interchange with the Class I railroads stops on those 22 railroads
manual_workaround: Host territory: operate under 236.1029(b) speed limits and absolute blocks set by the dispatcher; tenant territory: hold trains at the interchange or hand cars to Class I crews by agreement
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-03 (wayside interface units, radio); SYS-04 (train consists); SYS-06; SYS-08
dependent_third_parties: PTC software vendor; operator of the industry interoperable messaging network; Class I railroads and passenger operators (PTC back office peers)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Train control systems team (24/7 help desk); NOC
quantified_impact_basis: Interchange revenue at risk on 22 railroads (about $2.2 million a day) plus passenger host performance penalties and recovery costs (about $0.4 million)
single_points_of_failure: Industry interoperable messaging network (cannot be removed); PTC key management depends on 2 trained people

business_process: CTC signal control and wayside monitoring
description: CTC code servers and field code units, crossing remote health monitoring (1,140 crossings), 640 wayside detectors, and 9 machine vision portals reporting to the NOC
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Signals fail safe, but without CTC control the dispatcher cannot set routes and trains wait at red signals. Crossing health alarms and detector alarms stop reaching the NOC, so a failed crossing or a hot bearing depends on crews and radio announcements alone. Safety sets a short MTD
manual_workaround: Local control of interlockings by signal maintainers; detectors also announce to the passing train by radio; crews report crossing problems by radio; maintainers patrol monitored crossings in the affected region
dependent_third_parties: Crossing monitor vendor (cellular service); radio equipment vendor; telecommunications carriers
quantified_impact_basis: Train delay on 11 signaled railroads (about $0.8 million a day) plus maintainer overtime and patrols (about $0.3 million)
single_points_of_failure: Crossing monitor vendor cellular modems (outside PAM, gap 4)

description: Calling about 2,900 crew starts a day, tracking rest and hours of service, and keeping hours-of-service records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No train runs without a rested, called crew. Crew callers can work from printed boards for one shift; after 12 hours missed calls and hours-of-service errors rise. Records are written continuously
manual_workaround: Printed crew boards every 4 hours; calls by company mobile phone; paper hours-of-service records entered later
dependent_third_parties: Hosted crew calling telephony provider; Cloud provider A
dependent_people_or_facilities: Crew callers at the NOC; crew offices
quantified_impact_basis: About 20% of train starts missed after the first shift (about $2.3 million) plus overtime (about $0.1 million)
single_points_of_failure: Hosted crew calling telephony provider (fallback untested, gap 8)

business_process: Car management, waybilling, and interchange EDI
description: TMS: car location, waybills, train consists, interchange EDI with Class I railroads, RSSM car location data, demurrage records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cars can move for about a day on paper waybills and the last consist export, but Class I railroads need EDI to accept cars in normal volume, and PTC initialization needs current consists. RSSM location data must stay available for TSA (BP-06)
manual_workaround: Paper waybills; last consist export; car lists sent to Class I railroads by secure email
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; Class I railroads (EDI); industry car and waybill data exchange
quantified_impact_basis: Interchange refusals and car hire on about 5,200 carloads a day (about $1.5 million) plus demurrage and rework (about $0.3 million)
acquired_railroad_dependency: AQ-04 to AQ-06 send car events by file upload
single_points_of_failure: Cloud provider A region (second region available)

description: Security Coordinators reachable 24/7; RSSM car location answers to TSA within 30 minutes; chain of custody for RSSM cars; reports of significant security concerns to TSA; CISA reports by Covered Railroads
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A TSA location request can arrive at any hour and must be answered within 30 minutes (49 CFR 1580.203(d)); a cyber attack must be reported to TSA within 24 hours (1570.203). The fallback must always be ready, not recovered
manual_workaround: Printed RSSM car list every 4 hours at both NOCs (planned, gap 6); standby laptop with an offline extract; chain-of-custody forms on paper
dependent_third_parties: None for the duty itself; Cloud provider A for the data
quantified_impact_basis: Not revenue: exposure to TSA civil penalties and loss of TSA confidence; the value is a planning allowance
acquired_railroad_dependency: AQ-05 (CR-10) RSSM data sits in its legacy system
single_points_of_failure: TMS is the only electronic source of RSSM location data

business_process: Customer portal, car ordering, and shipment tracking
description: Web portal and APIs for about 4,800 shipper users: car orders, shipment tracking, releases, invoices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers can order cars by phone and email for two days; after that order backlog and complaints grow
manual_workaround: Car orders by phone and email to customer service; daily tracking reports by email
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; content delivery and web application firewall service
quantified_impact_basis: Lost and delayed car orders and customer service overtime

business_process: Track, bridge, and signal inspection and maintenance records
description: Inspection records under 49 CFR part 213, bridge inspections, signal tests, work planning, and slow orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Inspections are visual and continue on paper; only recordkeeping and planning depend on IT. Slow orders are also issued through dispatch bulletins (BP-01)
manual_workaround: Paper inspection forms; slow orders by dispatch bulletin
dependent_systems: Maintenance-of-way application (Cloud provider A); SYS-09 (tablets); SYS-06

business_process: Mechanical inspections, locomotive telematics, and onboard PTC maintenance
description: Locomotive and car inspection records, locomotive telematics and fuel data, onboard PTC apparatus troubleshooting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Inspections continue on paper. Onboard PTC troubleshooting needs the PTC back office (BP-02); equipped locomotives keep running while their units stay operative
manual_workaround: Paper inspection records; locomotive event recorder downloads kept locally
dependent_systems: Mechanical application (Cloud provider A); SYS-02; SYS-09
dependent_third_parties: Locomotive telematics vendor; PTC software vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Locomotives held for inspection paperwork and delayed repairs

business_process: Rail services: industrial switching and transload terminals
description: Switching at 38 customer plants and 12 transload terminals, with terminal operating systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers can be served from paper switch lists for two days; terminal truck scheduling by phone
manual_workaround: Paper switch lists; truck appointments by phone
dependent_people_or_facilities: Rail services crews and terminal staff
quantified_impact_basis: About 35% of rail services revenue ($1.6 million a day) at risk

business_process: SL-1 hosted PTC back office service for unaffiliated railroads
description: Hosted PTC back office tenants for 27 unaffiliated short lines (310 of their locomotives) on SYS-02
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer contracts commit to a 4-hour RTO and 15-minute RPO. Customer trains that need PTC cannot initialize for Class I territory while the service is down
manual_workaround: Customers hold trains at interchange; status calls every 2 hours from the service desk
dependent_third_parties: PTC software vendor; operator of the industry interoperable messaging network
dependent_people_or_facilities: Technology services team; train control systems team
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits under the SL-1 contracts and customer recovery support
single_points_of_failure: Shares the PTC back office with BP-02 (same recovery gap)

business_process: SL-2 dispatch and car management platform for unaffiliated railroads
description: Tenants on the CAD and TMS platforms for 18 short lines and industrial railroads
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer contracts commit to a 4-hour RTO and 15-minute RPO; customers rely on it for movement authority on their own track
manual_workaround: Customers fall back to their own paper track warrant procedures; company dispatch supervisors assist by phone
dependent_third_parties: CAD software vendor; Cloud provider A
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits under the SL-2 contracts and customer recovery support

business_process: Revenue accounting, billing, interline settlement, and collections
description: Freight billing, interline revenue settlement with connecting railroads, collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Billing can wait one weekly cycle; interline settlement runs monthly. Cash flow, not operations, drives the MTD
manual_workaround: Billing held and released later; manual invoices for top 20 customers
dependent_third_parties: ERP and revenue accounting vendor; banks
quantified_impact_basis: Cost of deferred collections and rework on about $13.2 million of daily revenue

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees under collective bargaining agreements, Railroad Retirement reporting, HR records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs weekly or every two weeks by craft. A missed payroll has labor relations and legal impact; the prior run can be repeated
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll and true up
dependent_third_parties: Payroll and HR SaaS vendor; banks
quantified_impact_basis: Labor claims, penalty pay, and rework

description: Monthly close, quarterly Form 10-Q and annual Form 10-K, disclosure controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: In the quarter-end window the MTD drops to 48 hours because of SEC filing deadlines
manual_workaround: Close from exported ledgers on standby laptops
dependent_systems: SYS-10; SYS-07 (Cloud provider B, reporting data)
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and the cost of a late filing risk in the quarter-end window

business_process: Dispatch on acquired railroads AQ-04 to AQ-06
description: Movement authority on the 3 acquired railroads still on their own legacy dispatch systems, run by local dispatchers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same safety basis as BP-01. Legacy systems have nightly backups only and no standby, so the real RPO is 24 hours and the vendors commit to next-business-day support. CR-10 (AQ-05) carries RSSM in an HTUA
manual_workaround: Paper track warrants by local dispatchers
dependent_systems: Legacy dispatch systems at AQ-04 to AQ-06; local directories; site VPNs
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 40 local dispatchers and clerks; 21 field sites
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of the 3 railroads revenue (about $0.75 million a day) at risk
single_points_of_failure: Each legacy dispatch server is a single point of failure

description: FRA accident/incident reports (part 225), hazmat incident reports (49 CFR 171.15), TSA and CISA reports, PTC failure reports to host railroads
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Telephone reports have hour-level clocks but can be made by phone without IT; written reports have 30-day windows
manual_workaround: Telephone reports from the NOC; paper logs
quantified_impact_basis: Penalty exposure; the value is a planning allowance
